report.plain_answer: Only one real disk cleanup was ever set up. On 28 Sep a Claude session cleaned the server by hand (95% down to 69%) and installed two guards: nightly PM2 log rotation and a 1 GB cap on the system journal. It also stopped VibeJob writing its bot token to the logs thousands of times a day. I checked them on the server today. The journal cap works, the token spam is gone and rotation runs every night. But the 'compress' setting has silently never worked (0 of 107 old files are zipped), and the install left behind an 842 MB old PM2 log that nothing will ever clean up. Those guards are not why the disk filled. They only cover two kinds of log, and in the next ten days about 14 GB of film and promo work landed where no tool looks: 7.2 GB of promo-film folders, about 2.9 GB for film #9, and 2.9 GB of scratch in /tmp (a 1.3 GB VibeJob test copy and 1.2 GB of music separations). No film or promo script checks free disk or removes its own working files; the 8 Oct guard checks RAM, not disk. The disk alarm did exist: a script checks the disk every 5 minutes and wrote 'WARNING: High disk usage' hundreds of times, but only into a file on the server that nobody reads, so you were never told. The rules that stop agents deleting other sessions' files did their job, but the 'check each film folder' step they wait on was never done. Had the 7.6 GB flagged on 28 Sep been checked and cleared, the disk would have peaked around 86% instead of 100%. The fixes I propose for your go mostly repair what already exists: a Telegram message when the disk crosses 85%, working compression, a 'close out the film' step once the final film is safely on your laptop, and a list of folders for you to approve one by one (up to about 15 GB). In interview words: this was an 'alarm with no listener' combined with 'fixing the incident instead of the class' — we capped what filled the disk last time, not the kind of growth that came next.

DOES NOT COVER: film folders (about 7.6 GB, flagged for a per-film check), /tmp, backups, /var/log/oracle-health.log, the journal at that step. This was a cleanup run by hand, not a tool. findings.claim: The only standing tooling ever put in place. (1) pm2-logrotate 3.0.0: max_size 50M, retain 10, compress, daily 00:00 UTC. (2) Journal capped through /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/99-aideazz-size.conf SystemMaxUse=1G, which brought it from 2.1 GB to 1010 MB. DOES NOT COVER: /tmp, the film/promo working folders (~/atuona-film*, ~/aigo-*), demucs stems, test copies, ~/.cache, backups, cron-written logs (/var/log/oracle-health.log, oci-keepalive.log), or files apps write themselves (VJH daily logs, espaluz-webhook.log, ~/logs/*). findings.topic: espaluz-webhook crash-loop known since 16 Jul, never disabled
findings.claim: The old espaluz-webhook.service runs the same paypal_webhook_server.py on :5000 that espaluz-payments-webhook already owns, so it crash-loops. The 16 Jul audit counted 154,000+ restarts and called 'systemctl disable' safe 'in a future pass, not urgent'. On 29 Sep it was 'seen, not touched'. It was never disabled. hist.summary:
Only one piece of disk tooling was ever encoded. On 28 Sep a Claude session ran a manual cleanup (c952a81), then installed two guards (58b90ec): pm2-logrotate (50M, retain 10, compress, daily) and a 1 GB journald cap (/etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/99-aideazz-size.conf), plus VJH b38836e (httpx to WARNING). The cleanup compressed logs and cleared npm/pip caches, taking the disk from 95% to 69% (about 11.8 GB freed).

It did not work for four reasons.

1. **It fixed that day's cause, not the one that came next.** On 28 Sep the disk was full of PM2 logs and journal. The guards cover only ~/.pm2/logs and the systemd journal. From 30 Sep to 8 Oct about 14 GB was filled by things the guards never covered:
   - four new promo-film folders (~/aigo-promo, -villa, -reloc, -med, about 7.3 GB);
   - demucs stems and a 1.3 GB VJH test copy in /tmp (4.0 GB);
   - the film #7/8/9 working folders (about 5 GB).

   No film or promo script checks free disk or removes its own intermediates. The 8 Oct '2.5 GB free' guard checks RAM, not disk.

2. **Nothing watches the disk.** check_oracle_health.sh only checks that processes are alive. health_monitor.sh writes disk warnings to its own file, and nothing shows it was ever scheduled. No code alerts on free space. The NOW.md start-of-session check has no df step. No disk reading was recorded between 28 Sep and 8 Oct, so 100% was only discovered during the RAM freeze.

3. **Unrotated logs and a known crash-loop.** /var/log/oracle-health.log (212 MB) is written by our own health script every 5 minutes and nothing rotates it. espaluz-webhook.service has crash-looped since at least 16 Jul (154,000+ restarts) because espaluz-payments-webhook already holds port 5000. 'Disable it' was noted as safe but never done (16 Jul, 29 Sep). Our health script and our Restart=always drop-in restart it every 5 minutes, which feeds the 290 MB espaluz-webhook.log. VJH also writes a new DEBUG log file every day (99 files) that nothing prunes.

4. **The fix was never confirmed or kept as code.** The pm2-logrotate and journald settings exist only on Oracle and as prose in NOW.md, in no repo. The 'VERIFY tomorrow' check that rotated files appeared was never recorded. That item was buried around line 1,120 of a 3,137-line NOW.md, and the memory line 'pm2-logrotate + journal 1G cap live' made the problem look solved.

The never-wipe and per-film-check rules worked as intended: every session (22 Sep, 28 Sep, 8 Oct, 9 Oct) found the space and deferred to Elena. But the per-film check was never actually done, and no one brought her a concrete delete list until 8-9 Oct, so 'waiting for her go' became permanent while new folders kept arriving.

There is also drift: the repo copy of the health script still has the broken pre-25-May dragontrade loop that was patched only on the live box. Redeploying from the repo would bring back a restart every 5 minutes and more log noise.

Current state (9 Oct): 98% used, 1.4 GB free. About 4.3 GB of candidates are listed in docs/atuona/FILM9_HANDOVER_2026-10-08.md:264-266, waiting for Elena's go. I changed nothing anywhere: everything above comes from git history, memory and the repo, and I did not touch Oracle.

live.summary:
I checked Oracle's live state read-only on 9 Oct 2026, 10:09–10:20 UTC. Nothing was deleted, truncated, restarted or edited. Side effect: running `cat` on the 8 /tmp/espaluz_video_*.mp4 files (170 MB) to measure them refreshed their access time, so the 30-day /tmp cleaner will now remove them about 8 Nov instead of about 27–30 Oct.

Disk now: 45G total, 43G used, 1.4G free (98%). Uptime 149 days (booted 13 May). No swap.

VERDICT: two of the three 28 Sep fixes held. The journal cap works (1015.5M, at or under 1G). pm2-logrotate does rotate daily and does enforce retain=10. The disk did not refill from logs. It refilled from about 13.5 GB of new film/promo working files, which no cleanup tool covers:
- ~/aigo-promo, aigo-med, aigo-villa, aigo-reloc, aigo-ig, aigo-art: about 7.2 GB, all created 30 Sep–4 Oct.
- ~/atuona-film9: 1.83 GB, created 6 Oct.
- /tmp: demucs music separations 1.16 GB, and a VibeJob test copy (vjh-test-20261006) of 1.22 GB.
- /var/www/influencer-images: +0.37 GB on 3–4 Oct.

Nobody was warned, because the only disk alert is health_monitor.sh. It writes 'WARNING: High disk usage' to ~/health.log, a file nobody reads; all 500 warning lines in its 1000-line window fired with no Telegram alert. The disk hit 100% on 8 Oct around 21:00 UTC.

The 28 Sep tooling also has four defects of its own:
1. pm2-logrotate's compress=true has silently never worked. pm2-logrotate 3.0.0's parseBool only accepts the string 'true', and pmx's Autocast turns that string into the boolean true first, so compression falls back to off. Result: 0 of 107 rotated files are gzipped. The 28 Sep NOW.md said 'VERIFY tomorrow: rotated *__*.log.gz files exist', and that check was never done.
2. When the module started, it moved the 842 MB pm2 daemon log to ~/.pm2/pm2__2026-09-28_15-38-05.log, uncompressed. That file will never be cleaned up: pm2.log only rotates at 50 MB and it is now 52 KB, so the 10-file retain limit is never reached.
3. The npm/pip cache clean was one-off, and ~/.cache/pip has already grown back 244.5 MB.
4. The 28 Sep work never looked at /var/log. Its app logs have no logrotate rule: espaluz-webhook.log 278 MB, oracle-health.log 203 MB, espaluz-familybot.log 138 MB, joblist-pipeline.log 2.5 MB.

The repeating 'espaluz-webhook not active, restarting' line is a separate problem, a stale duplicate service. espaluz-payments-webhook.service was written at 2026-06-28 11:32. Its process (pid 1031872, started 1 Oct) runs the same paypal_webhook_server.py on port 5000. The old espaluz-webhook.service was never disabled, so it has been failing with 'Address already in use' every ~10.25 s since 2026-06-28 11:32:56 (NRestarts=4352). The 5-minute health check restarts it again each time (29,634 times so far). That is about 245 MB of espaluz-webhook.log, ~2.3 MB/day, plus about half of all syslog systemd lines.

The resilience.conf drop-ins were meant to stop restart loops like this, but they put StartLimitIntervalSec in the [Service] section. Systemd logs 'Unknown key name StartLimitIntervalSec in section Service, ignoring', so the limit is the default 10s and can never trip.

oracle-health.log is big, but not because of this loop. 209.5 MB of its 212.9 MB was written before 26 May (pm2 status tables dumped during the old dragontrade restart loop), and it has grown only 312 KB since 28 Sep.

Space Elena could approve freeing (not touched): pm2 daemon log 842 MB; /tmp vjh-test 1.25 GB; /tmp demucs 1.19 GB; espaluz-webhook.log crash output about 245 MB; old logs of apps no longer in pm2, 331 MB (this includes the Bybit/Binance .gz, 273 MB, which memory says to keep).

findings.claim: The only disk monitor is health_monitor.sh (cron */5). It writes 'WARNING: High disk usage' (threshold 80%) to ~/health.log only: no Telegram, nobody reads it, and it keeps only the last 1000 lines (about 3.5 days). Every run in that window warned (500 warnings). Disk went from 95% at 2026-10-07 16:35 to 100% at 2026-10-08 21:00, then 98% after the 1.1 GB deletion. No other script checks df
findings.evidence: cat ~/health_monitor.sh -> 'if [ $DISK_PERCENT -gt 80 ]; then echo ... WARNING: High disk usage ... >> $LOG_FILE' and 'tail -1000 $LOG_FILE'; grep -c 'WARNING: High disk' ~/health.log -> 500 of 1000 lines; transitions: '2026-10-07 16:00 DISK: 95%', '2026-10-08 20:00 98%', '2026-10-08 21:00 100%', '2026-10-09 00:00 98%'; grep for df/DISK in ~/*.sh ~/bin/* ~/cto-aipa/scripts -> only health_monitor.sh; root crontab: 'no crontab for root'; /etc/cron.d has only certbot, e2scrub_all, sysstat
